content.text: The verifier confirms the classification is correct; the failed deterministic checks are artifacts of there being no covenant to measure. I'll restate the finding to make that explicit.

input.quote: This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative.
input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant exists anywhere in the agreement: targeted searches for "solicit", "hire", "induce", and "personnel" return nothing on point, and the only personnel-related provisions impose no hiring restraint (§ 5.4 merely requires each Party to appoint a General Manager as liaison; § 10.2 disclaims any employment/agency relationship). The restrictive covenants that do exist (§ 6 Exclusivity) concern competing web projects rather than employees, and § 6.3's two-year restraint binds HDI, not us, so it is outside this rule's scope and benefits our party. Because the rule's preferred position is the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer, that absence is compliant rather than missing. The duration-limit and general-solicitation carve-out checks are inapplicable — there is no covenant to measure them against — so no redline or comment is proposed.
